ComForce
Connect

Helping Milwaukee families stay in touch with the people arranging their care.

Andrew Bieber, Peter Gerrits, Asher Jaenchen, Zachary Millmann, Jesse Rost, Elton Emini

Who is following up with this family?

Fictional resident in Harambee

“Could someone check in with us? We also need a ride to meet our outreach worker.”

A family can ask
for both at once

The family gets one reference number. They choose when and how they feel comfortable hearing from a worker.

Example contact instructions

Text after 4 p.m. Please skip voicemail.

Who will call the family back?

When another worker takes over, they can see who promised to call and whether the family is still waiting for a ride.

Asking for help
in your own words

For residents

A parent can type “I need a ride” even if they don’t know the program’s name. They decide what to send.

For staff

After a conversation, a worker can ask for help drafting a note and check that it reflects what the family said.

What happened after the call?

01

Referral sentA worker contacts a partner about the ride.

02

Check-in completedA worker records the family conversation.

03

Need fulfilledStaff confirm the ride and record who provided it.

A pilot shaped by ComForce

Listen to a family

Invite a resident to try a fictional request. Which questions feel comfortable? Which would make them hesitate?

Walk with a worker

Try a busy shift on paper. When a ride falls through, can the next worker pick up where their colleague left off?

Ask what helped

Check how long the family waited for a reply and whether they received the help they asked for.

Thank you,
ComForce MKE

When a loved one is missing, a ride can mean being there for the next conversation. A promised call matters, too.
